texts.value: Mitochondrial phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase that catalyzes the conversion of oxaloacetate (OAA) to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), the rate-limiting step in the metabolic pathway that produces glucose from lactate and other precursors derived from the citric acid cycle (PubMed:28955899). Can play an active role in glyceroneogenesis and gluconeogenesis (PubMed:28955899). In lipogenic cells such as adipocytes, it generates PEP via the mitochondrial pyruvate-to-PEP bypass, driving the PEP flux required for cytosolic glycerol 3-phosphate and triglyceride synthesis (By similarity). Also acts as a serine/threonine-protein kinase: phosphorylates and activates ACSL4, thereby promoting ferroptosis (PubMed:38720107)
Binds 1 Mn(2+) ion per subunit.
kcat is 32 sec(-1) with oxaloacetate as substrate. kcat is 585 sec(-1) with phosphoenolpyruvate as substrate.

disease.description: Metabolic disorder resulting from impaired gluconeogenesis. It is a rare disease with less than 10 cases reported in the literature. Clinical characteristics include hypotonia, hepatomegaly, failure to thrive, lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia. Autopsy reveals fatty infiltration of both the liver and kidneys. The disorder is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.
